Really enjoyed this game. Can't wait to see future updates. I think really there's only about 20 hours of gameplay that feels like you're progressing. Then once You have a fast counter clerk and restock clerk, it basically turns into a game where you're just opening card packs. Which is fun at first but then becomes a bit repetitive. Give us more to do in the end game, so it feels less like the whole game is automated.

Things I'd like to see:
-Random events like shop lifting, employees calling off work. (could add security camera upgrades, and theft prevention employees)
-Add weather
-Trading, have NPC's come in with their own cards you can buy or trade for.
-Make it so the card game is actually playable, and you can compete with other NPC's for prizes.
-Make a menu that makes it clear what cards I have and what I'm missing in my collection. Would love to see a 'X cards owned / Out of X cards total' label.
-Instead of manually having to look at how much product you have, you should be able to just see a list of how much of each product that you have. Maybe even set it up where certain products are automatically reordered if they get below a certain threshold.
-More statistics. I want to see my profit breakdown per item. I want to see my past 10 days item costs, item earnings, etc.

I think my favorite part of the game is the fact that you'll see your players emote in the corner after clearly losing a game and then will stand up and rip $150 on packs.

Completely ignoring how good this title is as a video game, I want to instead highlight the fact that it's the full addiction loop of TCGs for less than the price of McDonald's. I did, however, spend almost 50 hours in 3 days opening boxes of cards, and you better believe I got a few nice foils in my display case.

All of that aside, this is what we would have without the MTX / P2W market that's overtaken gaming. That dopamine buzzer used to be quite a bit cheaper.

Basic gameplay loop is very simple - order products from the supplier, stick them on the shelves, set pricing, and then man the till.   Very simple and easy to follow.

But then it adds in a few other mechanics:
-Some customers come in stinky and you have to spray them with deodorant lol
-You can expand the store/display shelves/etc
-You can setup gaming tables for customers to play at and collect money passively from each table
-You can hire staff to man the till and restock shelves
-You can tear open card packs and sell the individual cards

The graphics aren't the greatest but it's a very satisfying game to play and I highly recommend it.  

It's absolutely worth the money.

Is this a 300hr game? It really shouldn't be, and I figure for some it's not even appealing in the first place. But I kept coming back to it, and you might too...

I think the dev really hit on a good thing. A combination of middle-complexity shop management, manual FPS running-around jobs and busywork, and of course the gacha mechanic that is soooo addictive (to be clear you dont actually pay for anything extra in this game, it's the mechanic of opening cards packs and boxes that gets that gachamine flowing) 

So, a Poke-based card shop with really good ancillary mechanics and plenty of variation, a really well constructed progression curve and a really, really impressive "one more day" captivation. It really is addictive, I think because while being a lazy game it still gives a ton of different things to do and improve on, that makes you want to do and improve on. 

The game's still in early access but is already fully fledged to play and enjoy, and I feel the dev is committed to further improvements including player suggestions. So there's really not much not to like. And I want to praise the dev a little, it really is nicely polished and turned out in all areas, clearly they don't let broken things in and IMO there's a lot going on to keep working well - my kudos for that.

So here's the big warning: if you don't like shop management games, or pokemons or never opened a packet of stickers or cards (sports ones will do), don't like dopamine, hate the idea of spraying stinky visitors to your shop with deodorant and then earning better ways to automate the stink out of these repulsive greebos, can't imagine getting fun from organising shelves then re-organising them, don't like comic books or plushies or DnD references, and only want to pew-pew, then please don't buy this excellent game.

I bought this game thinking it’d be one of those “play for 2 hours and forget about it” simulator games. Somehow I looked up and had 30+ hours in it, reorganizing shelves at 2AM like my life depended on it and ripping open packs in the back room like a full blown addict.

This game has absolutely NO right being this addictive.

It starts simple: stock shelves, sell cards, make money. Then suddenly you’re optimizing shelf layouts, chasing rare pulls, and judging customers the second they walk through the door. Watching your tiny shop slowly turn into a legit card store is insanely satisfying.

The pack opening system is dangerous too. Whoever designed it knew exactly what they were doing. Pulling a rare card hits like a dopamine nuke and next thing you know you opened half your inventory instead of selling it.

What really surprised me is how authentic the game feels. It somehow captures the exact vibe of a real local card shop,  the chaos, the excitement of big pulls, awkward customers, and the constant grind to keep everything stocked.

Huge respect to the devs because this feels like a game made by people who actually care. I kept saying “one more hour” and suddenly it was 4AM.

10/10 simulator.
Avoid if you value sleep.

I have to admit it's odd wanting to give this game a try, considering in my real life I own a LGS. I guess, I was interested to see how similar it was to the real thing. Here are my pros and cons list for TCG CSS.

Pros
* This is significantly more relaxing game than the pure amount of stress of running a real card shop. 

* TCG CSS is easy to pick up, learn and micro managing is even easier. I do find myself doing a lot of things I should leave my employees to do but I can't help it. 

* Dealing with smelly people is the biggest truth and similarly compared to real life.

* Opening packs sort of scratches that itch, you want to get those big hits! 

Cons
* I would like to see a lot more variety in products. I'd also like to see products show up for a limited time and then go away. I'd like to see allocation of products based on how much you ordered of certain items in the past. I'd like to see multiple distributors with different pricing. That way you could focus on one distro for better pricing or multiple for a better variety of products. There's a lot that can be done with this aspect of the game.   

* Employees will often go hangout outside as if they have nothing to do. I haven't been able to pinpoint exactly what causes this, but it's frustrating at times. They seem to not want to do their secondary tasks or in certain cases, their primary task.

* If your checkout counter or anywhere really where your character stands near a wall and customers are trying to go behind you, they'll often get stuck in the wall. This will sometimes also cause you to have to end the day prematurely even if it's in the middle of a transaction at your checkout counter.

* I wish you could decide which direction your shop can expand, it drives me crazy I can only add more space in one direction. Why can't we decide which direction? 

* Customers will get "stuck" at a play table waiting for a second person to sit down. This doesn't cause any issues, but does look silly after 9pm.

* I don't quite understand market price in this game, I believe at the start the games tells you something about charging a little above market price to sell something. My thought is, that's a little odd. That's generally what you'd say about something like MSRP (Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price) not market price. In my experience market price is significantly higher and is already a much higher price than purchased price or suggested price. All I'm thinking about is, it's sort of misleading to how we treat market price in the real world.  

* Speaking of market price, I'm also a little confused why the prices of everything fluctuate so much each day? Why are board games, playmats, deck boxes, sleeves etc changing in price so rapidly?  I completely understand cards and decks, but everything else shouldn't change much. Is this a way to create the "look" of supply and demand? I don't like it. This could be a huge improvement to the game, if there were actually a limited supply of items then prices would shift based on that.    

* Once you start getting to the end of the game, things fall pretty flat. I think this also hurts replay-ability in the long run. If you started a fresh run, the only differences will be how you design your store. I don't think that's enough for me once I've finished my current store run.  

* The thing that drives me the must nuts though, are customers coming up to the check out counter and wanting to trade for cards you don't have. What a massive waste of time, and this occurs too many times through out the day. I'm also not a fan of customers wanting you to buy cards under 0.50. That's a huge waste of the player's time. These things need to be removed from the game. 

* My final issue is with grading system. Why on earth am I sending cards in to be graded and they are coming back anything less than a 7. It's completely random. It becomes more than a gamble, it becomes wow, that's stupid and I would never do that in real life because I have eyes and can see this would grade terribly. Cards should have conditions (pre-graded) and you should visibly be able to see them, especially on cards traded in by costumers. 

I know I know, it seems I had a lot more negative things to say than I did positive, but that's because I was mostly being overly critical. There are changes I'd like to see happen, but there's nothing to overall deter from having fun with TCG CSS in it's current state. I think I can say, I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes management games.

So, I downloaded TCG Card Shop Simulator thinking it would be some chill little tycoon game where I flip trading cards and vibe out. Next thing I know, I’m knee-deep in a black market binder full of fake Charizards, my best customer just stormed out because I priced his Goblin Paladin too high, and I forgot to order sleeves for the midnight launch. This ain’t just a game—it’s retail trauma with glitter.

You don’t battle in this game. You sell. You live and die by market trends, collector moods, and that one shady dude named “Mikey” who swears his cards are authentic even though the ink is still wet. You start with a rinky-dink shop, buy some packs, flip 'em, decorate your shelves, and slowly upgrade your store into the nerd mecca of your pixel town. And yeah, you’ll get weirdly emotionally attached to your display case.

There’s this weirdly satisfying loop to it. You open a new pack and it’s like: “Boom. Foil dragon.” Instantly your brain hits dopamine overdrive. Then you sell it, make a profit, and think, “Yeah, I could do this for real.” (Narrator: They could not.)

What really hooks you is how alive everything feels. Prices change, collectors come in with oddly specific demands, and events throw off your whole plan. Sometimes your inventory is hot garbage. Other times, you're sitting on a gold mine and don’t even know it until some collector rolls in foaming at the mouth for a discontinued promo card you shoved in a bargain bin.

Honestly, it’s kind of a rollercoaster. One minute you're rolling in cash, the next you're praying someone will buy your leftover bulk commons just so you can pay for rent. There’s no safety net. Just vibes and markups.

Also, shoutout to the random event where a customer tried to trade me a rare card and a sandwich for a full booster box. I said yes. No regrets.

If you’re into TCGs, hoarding shiny stuff, and the fantasy of running your own card shop without going into actual debt—this is your game. Just don’t expect to duel anyone. You’re not the champion. You’re the cashier. A stressed-out, overworked, under-caffeinated cashier. And it’s awesome.

TCG Card Shop Simulator is so addictive and fun! Before I bought the game I watched so many YouTubers playing this and it looked perfect to me, as I'm such a sucker for games in which you run a store. The game didn't disappoint but it was even grindy-er than I thought it would be based on what I saw streamers play. 

First of all, I'm blown away by the amount of detail that went into this game. Not only for the TCG cards and their special effects like foil or a line around the border but you can also choose your currency and the money changes in the register. And What I also loved to see is that the customers had their own bag as well as having shipping costs when you order new stock from the distributor. As those are things in a irl shop as well that matters. You don't get products to your store for free, there is always a catch. I can also see how showing how hard it is to get the special cards might also be an eye opener on how much money has to be spent irl to get those special types of cards as well, or how lucky you need to be. This is just a guess, as I don't collect or play any TCG irl as I hate the randomness and different seasons to let you spend more money.

The first 25 hours of TCG Card Shop Simulator were amazing. Working towards unlocking the next set of cards, hiring staff to take over some of your tastes, it is great and kept me going! However, at some point, the grindyness starts to creep in. Goals are getting further away, opening packs yourself doesn't give you as many new cards as before and some of the achievements are a long way to go. This might chance the further this game gets closer to the 1.0 release, as I know the dev has plans to add the option to play the tcg game itself and possibly loads of other things. Seeing how many updates there were already to improve things give my high hopes for it being less grindy in the end. 

Loads of the achievements you'll just get by playing the game. For only a few of them you might want to do something special as change your stock, or have staff fulfill different roles. The achievements that will take the longest are:
- 5k customers played in your store: This can be done faster by sending them away as soon as both sit down and start the game, as that will already count as playing in your store. 
- Shop level 100: Selling items and opening booster give experience, so this is just a matter of time. 
- Collect 2500 different cards: This is really grindy, especially with just the game without mods, as you can only hold 8 booster packs in your hand and the speed of opening is so slow and you need to hold/click a lot of times. There are mods to increase the speed of opening items and the amount of boosters you can hold. That way you can also do other things while working toward this achievement. 

I give TCG Card Shop Simulator 4 out of 5 stars. This would be higher if the game wasn't so so grindy in the end.

Genuinely a hooking and captivating game... for the first few hours. People say that most good "cozy" games nowadays need another gameplay type to mix in (You see this with Stardew, Rune Factory, Cult of the Lamb), and this game certainly has it in the CCG aspect, with said CCG also looping back into sales for singles. This is intuitive, and adds a nice collectathon element to the game as a whole.

But the game isn't really there yet. After maybe 5-8 hours the game the game simply simmers down (to the point it is not engaging), but still holds slight bits of ritualistic fun (the same way Candy Crush can be fun for the 1000th hour). I think the reason why this becomes less and less fun over time though, even what that type of fun existing, is that there is no challenge in a CCG. This is a core design problem, as the game simply lacks interesting decisions or goals that are fun to chase.

There are a lot of QoL issues that need to happen (which to be fair, is actively being worked on), but there also needs to be a redesign (or maybe simply just additions) to the core gameplay loop in the mid to late game. Further chase goals that aren't just Steam Achievements, more customer feedback that can help you adjust your shop (The review system is helpful, but needs to dilute this feedback better), and milestones that have much more impact so that players are rewarded for progressing through levels, and unlocking new items to sell. Simply put, unlocking items past the first several days is completely unrewarding. There's also an argument for the drop rates being too stingy, but I can imagine this would be resolved by a difficulty setting (which the dev intends to implement).

People will definitely enjoy this if they simply like a cozy game and enjoy gacha/lootbox opening. This could be a widely appealing game, but definitely needs more design work on progression and overall structure, which to be fair, is completely fine for an Early Access game. The time I had with this game was fun overall, but the latter half of my save feels like it wasn't worth my time, outside of some rare Steam Achievements.

I would likely revisit this game in the full release.

Recommended.

TCG Card Shop Simulator is one of those games that sounds simple on paper, but once the loop gets its hooks in you, it is very hard to stop playing. You open the shop, stock the shelves, adjust prices, deal with customers, upgrade the store, and somehow an hour turns into five without much effort.

The biggest highlight for me is still opening card packs. That part of the game captures the exact feeling it should. You are always chasing the next rare pull, the next expensive card, or the next piece of your collection. Even when I tell myself I am just going to open a few packs and get back to running the shop, I end up ripping through way more than planned. The different packs give the game a great sense of progression too, because there is always another set, another rarity, or another card that makes you want to keep going.

I also really love the tournament system. It adds a lot more life to the shop and makes it feel like you are not just running a retail space, but building an actual local card shop. Watching people come in, sit down, play, and keep the place active is surprisingly satisfying. It gives you another reason to organize the store well and makes the business feel more alive than just shelves and sales.

The game has a really strong balance between relaxing shop management and that addictive collectible-card chase. Stocking products, expanding the store, opening packs, selling singles, and hosting tournaments all feed into each other in a way that feels rewarding. There is always something small to improve, and that is exactly what makes it so easy to keep playing.

It is still a little grindy at times, and I would always love to see even more cards, more pack variety, and more ways to make tournaments feel deeper over time. But the foundation is excellent. If you enjoy shop sims, collecting games, or the simple thrill of opening card packs, this is very easy to recommend.

[b]Do not buy this if you want a shopkeeping/management sim game.[/b] There is 0 depth to the gameplay. There is no strategy around pricing, supply and demand, shop layout, customer behaviour, employee management, or any other mechanic you might expect of a shop sim.

It has the [i]appearance[/i] of those things (market prices change randomly day-to-day, customers supposedly can be unhappy), but none of it matters. You just buy anything, sell it around market price, and... that's it. Number go up, repeat the next day.

[b]This game is really about opening card packs.[/b] If you ever dreamt of working at a card shop as a kid, you probably imagined you could open card packs and play games all day. It only simulates part of that dream: you get to open unlimited card packs, but you can't actually play with them.

Unfortunately, it seems that the gacha/collection part with legally-distinct P*kemon cards is enough to tickle my brain for many hours.

The game really looks and feels amateur (can't escape that default Unity lighting, janky UI, basic UI/state bugs), but at least it seems to be made with genuine effort (unlike the majority of Unity job sim clones that are pure asset flips or LLM garbage).

There is an active modding scene now which might add some value for you.
